learning_outcomes.text: Identify and describe basic principles and methods of mechanical engineering applied to the CGM discipline.
Know and be able to explain the constructive principles and mechanical thermal schemes of the main types of machines.
Know the processes that occur in machines.
Know the main characteristics of machines.
Be able to compare different machines based on their technical characteristics.
Highlight the phenomena influencing the operation of machines.
Understand the characteristic curves of machines and explain operating particularities based on these curves.
Operate with basic methods and techniques from the field of machines and associate them with specific graphical representations, diagrams, characteristic curves.
Select and apply basic concepts, principles, and methods from the field for describing thermodynamic and mechanical schemes specific to different types of machines.
Select and apply criteria, principles, and methods for identifying thermodynamic, thermal, and mechanical phenomena and processes.
Select and analyze specific bibliographic sources in the field of machines.
Demonstrate autonomy in learning specific machine problems.

Respect ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrate into the work group and apply relationship and efficient teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously inform and document themselves in their field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.

syllabus_topics: 1.2. Machines. Power machines and working machines. Definitions. Machines in contemporary human life
1.3. Subject of the discipline General course of machines
Chapter 2. Theoretical bases of machine operation
2.1.1. Working agents. Thermodynamic system. Parameters and state equations
2.1.2. Mechanical work and heat in state transformations
2.1.3. Analytical expressions for mechanical work and heat
2.2.1. Formulations and expressions of the first principle of thermodynamics
2.3.2. Closed transformations. Thermal efficiency. Carnot cycle
2.3. Water vapor. Obtaining. p - v diagram. Parameters
2.4.3. Flow of gases and liquids through nozzles and diffusers
3.1.1. Linear piston compressor. Construction of a compressor
4.1. Construction and operation of a 4-stroke ICE. Classifications
4.2.1. Indicated diagram. Thermodynamic cycle Thermal efficiency
4.2.2. Mixture formation in SI ICE. Elementary carburetor. Gasoline injection
4.3. Compression Ignition ICE (CI ICE). Indicated diagram. Cycles
4.4. Supercharged ICE. Supercharging schemes. Turbochargers for supercharging. Indicated diagram of a 4-stroke supercharged ICE
4.5. Indicated and effective ICE parameters. Efficiencies
5.1. Constructive scheme and operation of a steam boiler
5.4. Energy balance of a steam boiler
6.1. Principle scheme of a power plant with steam turbine. Rankine thermodynamic cycle
6.2. Construction of a steam turbine (on the example of a combined turbine with Curtis-Rateau velocity and pressure stages)
6.3. Energy processes in the turbine stage
7.1. Gas turbine plant with constant pressure combustion. Constructive scheme
7.1.2. Cycle of the gas turbine plant with constant pressure combustion (Brayton)
7.2. Axial and radial gas turbine constructions
7.3. Uses of gas turbines: in thermal power plants, in aviation, for ICE supercharging
8.2. Single-stage mechanical vapor compression refrigeration plant
8.2.1. Constructive scheme. Role of component elements
8.2.2. Plant operation analyzed on p -i and T - s diagrams
9.1. Definitions. Classification. Scheme of a hydro-energetic node
9.6. Representative hydropower plants in our country equipped with different types of hydraulic turbines
10.2.1. Construction of a centrifugal pump. Operation
10.3.2. Axial piston pump. Construction and operation
10.1. Definitions. Classification. Main types of machine tools and tool types
10.2. Principle scheme of a universal lathe
10.3. Principle scheme of a milling machine
12.1. Principle constructive scheme of a car
12.2. Auxiliary systems and installations. Braking. Cooling. Fuel supply
1. SI, technical, and Anglo-Saxon units of measurement used in the study of machines. Pressure and temperature, fundamental parameters of machine operation
4. Construction of an internal combustion engine
5. Turbocharger for supercharging internal combustion engines
6. Construction of a steam turbine with velocity and pressure stages
7. Construction of a gas turbomotor (derived from aviation)
teaching_methods: Classic lectures, with exposition and presentation at the blackboard of the studied problems
Drawing sketches, describing physical mathematical modeling of studied phenomena, complete mathematical demonstrations when necessary
Short recap of notions discussed in the previous lecture
Interactive discussions with direct audience involvement
Seminar activities with exposition and presentation at the blackboard of the studied problems
assessment_rules: Conditions for promotion: minimum grade 5 for each discipline activity (colloquium, seminar). The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 10 to 1 are awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimal learning outcomes specific to a discipline and the granting of its corresponding study credits.
